Submit a request to a model endpoint, then poll for the result or receive a webhook when processing finishes. Run your first request Create credentials and complete a generation from submission to result. Get an API key Create and manage server-side credentials in Higgsfield Console. Make a request Every model uses the same authentication and asynchronous request lifecycle. The JSON body depends on the selected model. Start with Genjutsu motion transfer . Replace the example media URLs with publicly accessible URLs for your own video and reference image. The source video must be at least 4 seconds long. Nano Banana Pro Google Omni Flash Seedance 2.5 Seedream 5.0 Lite Seedance 2.0 Kling 3 GPT Image 2.5 Soul 2.0 Got any questions left? How does Higgsfield connect to AI agents? Higgsfield uses MCP (Model Context Protocol), an open standard that gives AI agents access to external tools. Once connected, your agent can generate images, create videos, train characters, and browse your creation history, all within a single session. Which agents are supported? Higgsfield MCP works with Claude (web, Cowork, and Claude Code), OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and NemoClaw. Any agent or client that supports MCP can connect to Higgsfield. What models are available? Higgsfield gives your agent access to 35+ models and tools including Soul, Cinema Studio, Flux, Seedream, Kling, Minimax Hailuo, Veo, and more. Your agent automatically selects the best model for the task, or you can specify one yourself. What can I create? Images up to 8K resolution, videos up to 30 seconds across multiple cinematic styles, consistent characters using Soul training, and more. You can generate from text prompts, reference images, or a combination of both. Do I need an API key? No. Add the Higgsfield MCP server URL in your agent's settings and authenticate through your Higgsfield account. No API keys to manage or configure. How does pricing work? Higgsfield tools use the same credit system as the Higgsfield platform. Each generation costs credits based on the model and resolution. Your existing Higgsfield plan credits work seamlessly through any connected agent. How long does generation take? Images typically complete in a few seconds. Videos take longer depending on duration and model. All generation runs asynchronously, so your agent polls for results and delivers them as soon as they're ready. Can I use previous generations as input? Yes. You can browse your full generation history, reference any past image or video, and use it as a starting point for new creations. This makes iterative workflows and multi-step production easy. Can I use Higgsfield with my own agent setup? Yes. Any MCP-compatible client can connect. If you're running OpenClaw on a VPS, Hermes Agent on your local machine, or NemoClaw on NVIDIA hardware, just point it to the Higgsfield MCP server and you're ready to generate. Navigation Get started Authentication Documentation API reference Enterprise Get started Overview Quickstart Authentication How the API works Core concepts Requests and lifecycle Idempotent requests Polling Webhooks File uploads Errors and retries Rate limits Billing and retention SDKs Client libraries Organizations Overview Managing members Resources FAQ Support close On this page Back to top Authorization header Keep credentials server-side Authentication errors Get started Authentication Copy page Copy page Authenticate server-side API requests with your Higgsfield key and secret. Copy page Copy page Create and manage API credentials in Higgsfield Console . Each credential consists of a key ID and a secret. Authorization header Send both values in the Authorization header: Authorization : Key YOUR_KEY_ID:YOUR_KEY_SECRET curl https://api.higgsfield.ai/requests/REQUEST_ID/status \ --header "Authorization: Key ${ HF_API_KEY_ID }:${ HF_API_KEY_SECRET }" The API also accepts the legacy hf-api-key and hf-secret headers. New integrations should use the Authorization header. Keep credentials server-side Do not call the API directly from browser or mobile application code. Anyone who can inspect the application can extract its API secret and use your account. Store credentials in a secrets manager or encrypted environment variables. Use separate credentials for development and production. Never include credentials in URLs, logs, screenshots, or support messages. Rotate a credential immediately if it may have been exposed. Authentication errors Missing, malformed, or invalid credentials return 401 Unauthorized : { "detail" : "Invalid credentials" } Authentication identifies the account, but individual models may have separate access restrictions. A model unavailable to the authenticated account can return 404 , 423 , or 503 depending on its operational state. Was this page helpful? Navigation Core concepts Rate limits Documentation API reference Enterprise Get started Overview Quickstart Authentication How the API works Core concepts Requests and lifecycle Idempotent requests Polling Webhooks File uploads Errors and retries Rate limits Billing and retention SDKs Client libraries Organizations Overview Managing members Resources FAQ Support close On this page Back to top When concurrency is reached When the queue is full Endpoint-specific limits Client recommendations Core concepts Rate limits Copy page Copy page Design integrations for account and model concurrency limits. Copy page Copy page Rate limits depend on the account and the selected model. View the limits assigned to your account in Higgsfield Console . The primary generation limit is concurrency: the number of requests that may be processing at the same time. Some models can also have model-specific limits. When concurrency is reached Generation requests above your concurrency limit are still accepted. The API returns a request_id with status queued , and the request starts automatically when one of your running requests reaches a terminal status. When the queue is full The number of generations waiting to start is limited too. The queue limit is a multiple of your account’s concurrency limit, and each output of a batch request counts separately. When the queue is full, a new generation request is rejected with 429 Too Many Requests and a Retry-After header, and nothing is created or charged: { "detail" : { "code" : "account_queue_full" , "message" : "Too many queued generations for this account" , "retryable" : true , "limit" : 40 , "retry_after_seconds" : 30 } } limit is the queue limit for your account. Wait for Retry-After seconds and submit again with the same Idempotency-Key ; queued requests leave the queue as soon as they start. If queue admission is briefly unavailable, the API returns 503 Service Unavailable with "code": "admission_control_unavailable" and "retryable": true . Retry with backoff. Endpoint-specific limits Some non-generation endpoints reject requests above their limit instead of queuing them. They return 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header: Endpoint Limit POST /v1/custom-references Number of Soul ID references training at the same time { "detail" : "Maximum number of concurrent requests (2) has been reached" } Client recommendations On 429 , wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After before submitting again. Limit generation submissions with a worker pool or semaphore so the queue stays short and never reaches its limit. Track each accepted request_id until it becomes terminal. Use backoff and jitter instead of retrying in a tight loop. Keep polling traffic separate from generation submission concurrency. Let us know in Discord before a planned traffic increase if you need higher limits. Successful responses do not yet include rate-limit headers with your remaining capacity. Treat the limits shown in your dashboard as the authoritative values for your account. Was this page helpful?
